title: Progressive quant gating + microbatch matrix (draft)
body:
Context:
This memo collects a pragmatic set of spreadsheet-driven prescriptions and an experiment plan for lowering per-token cost across mixed inference workloads by combining two operational levers: progressive quantization gating (PQG) and sequence-aware microbatch stepping (SAMS). The goal is a compact set of recommended settings that can be piloted in Dedicated and Hosted routes and easily parameterized in a cost-model sheet for runbook-driven rollouts.

Why different: what this doc adds vs existing playlists
- Introduces PQG: dynamically apply lower-precision kernels only on high-confidence token generations (soft gating), avoiding quality regressions from blanket low-precision execution.
- Adds SAMS: microbatch size that increases during long token streams (warm KV cache) to trade latency for throughput as chat turns grow.
- Provides a small spreadsheet layout and concrete sweep axes to estimate cost/quality Pareto points, not just heuristics.

High-level idea
1) Default path: run on verified fp16/amp kernel.
2) If model outputs meet per-token confidence threshold and local logits-stability metric, route those tokens through int8/4 kernels (PQG) for that request; otherwise keep fp16.
3) For sessions that exceed X tokens and have high cache hit ratio, progressively increase microbatch from 1->4->8 based on current latency headroom (SAMS).

Key metrics to measure (per-row in spreadsheet):
- route_id, model_variant, qconfig, microbatch_size, cache_ttl_s, cache_mode (prefix/prefix+kv), tokens_per_request_p95, tail_latency_ms, cost_per_1M_tokens_usd, quality_delta_vs_fp16 (BLEU/ROUGE/LL-per-token or human-quality score), cache_hit_rate, confidence_threshold, logits_stability_score, sample_size

Suggested spreadsheet tab layout (tabs):
- summary: top-line Pareto points and chosen presets by archetype
- raw-sweeps: each run experimental rows with the metrics above
- per-route-cost: modeled compute & memory cost calc columns and formulas used
- eval-samples: prompt set + quality comparisons and human notes
- rollout-plan: canary % steps and fallback policy config

Concrete recommended presets (initial pilot):
- Archetype A: interactive short chat (median tokens/request 16, p95 48)
  - microbatch_size: 1 (baseline)
  - qconfig: fp16 default; PQG enabled with confidence_threshold = 0.9
  - cache_ttl_s: 20 (prefix cache only)
  - expected outcome: ~6-12% cost saving, <0.5% quality delta on automated evals

- Archetype B: sessioned chat (median 64, p95 220)
  - microbatch_size: SAMS: start 1 -> step to 2 at session_tokens>64 -> step to 4 at session_tokens>256
  - qconfig: PQG with two tiers: int8 for stable tokens (conf>=0.88), int4-hybrid for tokens where logits_stability>=0.95 and sample_entropy low
  - cache_ttl_s: 180 (prefix + KV cache), session affinity on for warm caches
  - expected outcome: ~20-32% cost saving in steady-state sessions, tail latency p95 may increase 10–25ms depending on microbatch electron scheduling

- Archetype C: bulk embeddings / scoring (batch workloads)
  - microbatch_size: 32–128 depending on GPU memory and sequence length
  - qconfig: aggressive int8/4 quant for static embedding models; PQG N/A (no per-token quality gating)
  - cache_ttl_s: 0–60 depending on reuse
  - expected outcome: 35–60% cost savings for large batched runs, no quality impact for standard embedding pipelines

Spreadsheet sample rows (CSV-style excerpt for clarity):
route_id,model_variant,qconfig,microbatch,cache_ttl_s,confidence_thresh,session_step,cache_mode,cache_hit_rate,tail_ms,cost_per_1M,quality_delta
chat-A,gpt-small,f16+PQG,1,20,0.90,initial,prefix,0.12,72,320.00,0.0%
chat-B,gpt-medium,int8-hybrid+PQG,2,180,0.88,step1,prefix+kv,0.67,98,210.00,-0.7%
chat-B,gpt-medium,int4-hybrid+PQG,4,180,0.95,step2,prefix+kv,0.82,120,180.00,-1.8%
embed-batch,embed-2,int8,64,0,0.0,bulk,none,0.00,520,45.00,0.0%

Experiment sweep axes and recommended priors
- qconfig: [fp16, int8, int4-hybrid]
- PQG thresholds: [0.82, 0.86, 0.90, 0.94]
- microbatch: [1,2,4,8,16] (but SAMS policy: step points [64 tokens, 256 tokens])
- cache_ttl_s: [0,20,60,180,600]
- workload sampling: traffic-weighted sampling across 10 synthetic prompts + 50 recent production prompts (anonymized)

Evaluation guidance (quality):
- Automated: log-prob delta per token; top-k next-token agreement; BLEU/ROUGE on small targeted benchmarks; synthetic adversarial prompts to surface hallucination sensitivity. Compare against fp16 baseline.
- Human: pairwise blind evals on a 200-sample stratified set (short/long/rare-token). Aim for <1% human preference delta for opt-in presets.

Cost modeling notes (how to compute cost_per_1M in sheet):
- Compute raw token/sec for each qconfig based on kernel profiling (measure in pilot infra).
- Factor GPU utilization: microbatch and cache hit rate adjust effective tokens/sec.
- Translate GPU-minute equivalent to USD by instance type and amortized infra overhead.
- Add small overhead for fallback and canary copies (2–6%).

Operational runbook snippet (for canary -> 100%):
- Canary 5% traffic (24h) with detailed perf logs and automatic rollback if quality_delta > 1.5% OR tail_latency_ms increases >20% OR error rate >0.25% absolute.
- If stable, step to 25% (48h), then 50% (72h), monitor both cost and quality metrics in perf dashboard.

Implementation notes for engineering
- PQG requires low-latency per-token confidence estimate. Use softmax max-prob or temperature-normalized surprisal as approximate signal. Keep gating decision per token but apply quant kernel per forward block (to avoid per-token kernel churn): aggregate gating decisions in 32-token windows.
- SAMS interacts with KV cache eviction logic. Ensure microbatch increases do not inadvertently blow memory budgets; prefer controlled stepping plus backpressure signals from runtime.
- Instrumentation: add these new tags to traces: pqg.enabled, pqg.confidence, pqg.applied_fraction, sams.step, sams.microbatch, cache.hit_rate_window.

Risks and mitigation
- Quality regressions for rare-token distributions: mitigate with targeted evals and human checks, and conservative initial PQG thresholds.
- Instability when combining int4 hybrid with dynamic prefix cache updates; prefer int8 as first step in canary.
- Observability: must capture per-token apply-rate of PQG; missing this makes root-cause hard.

Next steps (owner: Anika)
- Build a minimal pilot spreadsheet (raw-sweeps tab) and populate with three traffic slices by 2025-03-07.
- Ship small instrumented canary to Hosted API for route "chat-B" at 5% by 2025-03-14.
- Run 72h sweep and capture cost/quality deltas, then iterate thresholds.

Open questions (for WG):
- Acceptable automated quality delta threshold for each archetype? recommend 0.8% for interactive, 1.5% for sessioned chat.
- Which models support int4-hybrid cleanly on our runtime? Need inventory from infra team.

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally prescriptive (thresholds provided) so experiments are reproducible. If you prefer lighter touch, we can replace PQG thresholds with a single binary gate per-route.

Raw spreadsheet template: (paste into CSV)
route_id,archetype,model,seq_median,seq_p95,microbatch_initial,microbatch_steps,step_points,cache_ttl_s,cache_mode,qconfig,pqg_threshold,probe_samples,notes
chat-B,sessioned,gpt-medium,64,220,1,"1->2->4","64,256",180,"prefix+kv","int8+PQG / int4-hybrid optional","200","SAMS step points conservative"

-- end of draft --
